title: Philadelphia Fed Fourth Quarter 2026 Price and Inflation Expectations Survey — 10:00 a.m. ET, the Third District's direct read on pass-through, sixteen days before the funding cliff
source: EST: philadelphiafed.org/calendar-of-events?release=manufacturing-business-outlook-survey — the Philadelphia Fed's own filtered release calendar, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 131,096 bytes). Its embedded structured data carries the row verbatim: 'Fourth Quarter 2026 Price and Inflation Expectations Survey | Nov 25 2026 | 10:00 a.m.' The instrument is described on the bank's MBOS landing page (HTTP 200, 277,555 bytes, same-day fetch) as a 'Quarterly survey of price and inflation expectations among manufacturing and nonmanufacturing firms in the Third District', last edition dated 26 Aug '26 — consistent with a late-November Q4 slot. Filed estimate on three counts: market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no member for a regional Reserve Bank's own survey schedule (FED: covers the federalreserve.gov FOMC calendar only), this lane never self-confirms an event it discovered in-sweep, and only the one calendar row was read — no separate release page for this survey was fetched. Discovered in the never-assessed initial research of philly-fed-mfg-2026-12-17, 2026-09-09
notes: PROPOSED (not canonical) by the philly-fed-mfg-2026-12-17 initial-research adjacency sweep on 2026-09-09. Filed because a sibling ledger NAMED this exact instrument and declined it for one stated reason that no longer holds. docs/research/events/philly-fed-mfg-2026-10-15.md's sweep records: 'The Third District Price and Inflation Expectations Survey (quarterly, next edition undated on the page fetched) — the most on-thesis instrument for the pass-through question, declined only because no date was obtainable from the primary today. Named, not guessed.' The date is now obtainable, read verbatim from the bank's own filtered calendar, and it is 2026-11-25. Why it matters to the corridor this proposer sits in: all three Philadelphia Fed ledgers on the shelf circle the same unanswered question — whether an energy shock (EIA regular gasoline $4.071/gal week-ending 2026-08-31, +28.1% y/y) is passing through to producer prices — and the MBOS can only ever answer it by direction-of-change diffusion, which the 10-15 ledger measured as a NOWCAST rather than a lead (Philly prices paid vs core PPI 3m annualized peaks at lead 0, r=0.637, decaying to 0.178 by six months). A survey that asks firms directly for expected price changes is the instrument that would carry forward information the MBOS structurally cannot. It also lands 16 days before government-funding-deadline-2026-12-11 (high, estimate) and, being Fed-funded, publishes through a lapse where BLS and Census do not. Impact LOW and symbols [] on the same grounds as every sibling Third District entry: a sub-state survey of a qualitative kind, no house playbook keyed to regional surveys, no tracked name carrying a Third District channel. Whoever writes the canonical file owns (a) re-verifying the date and the 10:00 a.m. time against a release page for this survey specifically rather than the shared calendar row, and (b) establishing what the survey actually publishes — the calendar row gives a title and a time and nothing about the series' content, history or availability. This is a PROPOSAL and an ESTIMATE — it widens caution, licenses nothing, and the proposing ledger registers no forward test that depends on it.
